trial_court: Civil Judge (Senior Division), Ghaziabad — Marriage Petition No. 679 of 2000
case_name: Smt. Shalu Sharma vs Ajay Sharma
facts_of_case: The petitioner filed a petition for divorce in the Court of the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Ghaziabad, which was registered as marriage petition No. 679 of 2000. The suit is tentatively valued at Rs. 1,00,000/- and court-fees have been separately paid.

legal_principles.principle: The valuation of a suit determines the jurisdiction of the Court and the forum for filing an appeal.
legal_principles.held: Thus the valuation of the suit is governed by the Suits Valuation Act; 1887. Sections 8 and 9 of the Suits Valuation Act are relevant for the purpose.

legal_principles.principle: When the subject-matter of suits is such that it does not admit of being satisfactorily valued, the High Court may direct that suits shall be treated as if their subject-matter were of a specified value.
legal_principles.held: Section 9 of the Suits Valuation Act provides:— '9. Determination of value of certain suits by High Court, ...... When the subject-matter of suits of any class other than suits mentioned in Section 4 or 8 is such that in the opinion of the High Court it does not admit of being satisfactorily valued, the High Court may, with the previous sanction of the State Government, direct that suits of that class shall, for the purposes of the Court-fees Act, 1870, and of this Act and any other enactment for the time being in force, be treated as if their subject-matter were of such value as the High Court thinks fit to specify in this behalf.'

outcome.final_order: The order dated 27-8-2002 passed by the XIII Additional District Judge, Ghaziabad is quashed.

use_for_drafting: quashing an order of the family court
filing a civil appeal against a judgment and decree
